title: Morph Target Demo (Sphere)
prompt:
Use Three.js to create a sphere mesh with 3 morph targets, providing weight sliders, an animation toggle, and a wireframe mode toggle.

[Three.js Import Method (Must Be Followed Strictly)]
Use the following importmap in <head>, and import via ES Modules in <script type="module">:
<script type="importmap">
{ "imports": {
    "three": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/build/three.module.js",
    "three/addons/": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/examples/jsm/"
} }
</script>
<script type="module">
import * as THREE from 'three';
import { OrbitControls } from 'three/addons/controls/OrbitControls.js';
</script>

[Geometry]
(1) SphereGeometry must have a sufficient number of segments (such as 32,32). On the BufferGeometry, duplicate and edit the position attribute to generate 3 morphAttributes.position attributes (for example, a conical protrusion, horizontal compression, and vertical elongation).
(2) Use MeshStandardMaterial or MeshPhongMaterial, with morphTargets: true.
(3) id="morphWeight0", id="morphWeight1", and id="morphWeight2": three <input type="range" min="0" max="1" step="0.01" /> elements that control morphTargetInfluences[0..2], respectively.
(4) id="animateToggle": a checkbox. When enabled, periodically change the weights using requestAnimationFrame (using sine waves or similar); when disabled, the weights are controlled only by the sliders.
(5) id="wireframeToggle": a checkbox that toggles material.wireframe.

[State Exposure (Required)]
window.__3D_STATE__ = {
  morphWeights: [number, number, number],  // Matches morphTargetInfluences; length is always 3
  animating: boolean,
  wireframe: boolean,
  vertexCount: number                      // Number of vertices in the sphere's position attribute
}

Output a single HTML file that can run when opened directly in a browser.
